subtopics.title: From Growth to Decay — the Two Depreciation Formulae

questions.question: The straight-line depreciation formula is:
A minibus of R360 000 depreciates straight-line at 12% p.a. After 5 years it is worth:
The same minibus on reducing balance at 12% p.a. for 5 years is worth:
A structural difference between the two models is that:
options: Straight line can never reach zero
Both reach zero at the same moment
Straight line reaches zero after 1 ÷ i years, while reducing balance never reaches zero

questions.question: For 8% p.a. compounded quarterly over 3 years, the correct i and n are:
R15 000 at 8% p.a. compounded quarterly grows in 3 years to:
At the same quoted rate, quarterly compounding beats annual compounding because:
options: The bank rounds up four times instead of once
The quarterly rate is larger than the annual rate
Each quarter's interest joins the principal immediately and starts earning interest itself
The formula uses a larger P each quarter for free

questions.question: The classic finance error this section warns against is:
options: Rounding the final answer to two decimals
Writing the conversion line before the formula
Using a calculator for the power
Mixing clocks — a quarterly rate with n in years, or an annual rate with n in quarters

questions.question: The effective annual rate of 8% p.a. compounded quarterly is about:
The law connecting effective and nominal rates is:
Bank X offers 8,3% compounded annually; Bank Y offers 8,1% compounded monthly. The better offer is:
options: Bank X, because 8,3 is bigger than 8,1
Bank Y, whose effective rate of about 8,41% beats 8,3%
It depends on the size of the deposit

questions.question: With compounding more than once a year, a computed effective rate BELOW the nominal rate means:
options: The bank pays no interest in December
The nominal rate was quoted in months
A power and a root swapped somewhere — effective must exceed nominal in that case

subtopics.title: Exchange Rates and Mixed Timeline Problems

questions.question: At R17,60 per dollar, a camera priced at $650 costs:
When the rand weakens from R17,60 to R18,40 per dollar, the same $650 camera:
options: Keeps its rand price, since the dollar price is unchanged
Costs R520 more in rand — how a weaker rand feeds inflation
Is no longer available for import

questions.question: One advantage of a WEAKER rand is that:
options: South African exports and tourism become cheaper for foreign buyers
Overseas holidays cost South Africans less

questions.question: R9 000 at 7% p.a. compounded quarterly for 4 years grows to:
In the ruler picture, straight-line depreciation removes:
options: 12% of the current value each year
The same fixed step of the ORIGINAL value every year

questions.question: The photocopy-of-a-photocopy picture captures reducing balance because:
options: Each generation keeps 88% of the ONE BEFORE, never of the original
The original picture is destroyed first
Copies are made only in December

questions.question: On reducing balance, the minibus loses R43 200 in year one but only about R25 900 in year five because:
options: 12% of a smaller current value is a smaller bite
Straight-line takes over in year five

questions.question: The keywords that signal the photocopier model in a question are:
In the paydays picture, quarterly compounding wins because:
options: Four paydays always contain more interest at a higher rate
March's interest is already earning by April instead of waiting for December
December interest is taxed more heavily

questions.question: Over 3 years on R15 000 at 8%, payday timing alone is worth about:
The clock-conversion rule for monthly paydays is:
options: Divide the rate by 4 and count quarters
Multiply the rate by 12 and count years
Divide the rate by 12 and count months
Keep the annual rate and count months

questions.question: The honest footnote about compounding frequency is that:
options: Beyond quarterly, extra frequency loses money
Each extra slicing helps less than the last — daily beats monthly by barely a cent

subtopics.title: The Headline and the Till Slip

questions.question: In the bank-window picture, the nominal rate is the headline poster and the effective rate is:
options: The till slip — what the year actually did to your money, fine print included
The poster of the rival bank

questions.question: The till slip is printed by:
options: Pushing one rand through a full year — for example 1,00675 twelve times over
Adding the twelve monthly rates together
Subtracting the fine print from the headline
Dividing the headline rate by the number of paydays

questions.question: Offers from different banks can only be compared fairly by:
options: Asking which bank has lower fees
Converting every offer to its effective rate and comparing those

questions.question: The camera's rand price rising from R11 440 to R11 960 while staying $650 shows that:
options: The shop increased its profit margin
A weakening rand raises the rand cost of imports even when foreign prices stand still
Exchange rates only matter to exporters
